instructions: Up to a day ahead, or weeks ahead if you plan to freeze them: Put the bulgur in a large bowl, cover it with cold water, and let it soak for 20 minutes. Drain it in a fine sieve and squeeze out as much water as you can.

Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 1 of the onions, chopped, and cook for 8 minutes, until golden. Add half of the lamb, 1/2 tsp of the seven-spice, 1/4 tsp of the black pepper and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Turn the heat to medium-high and cook for 6 minutes, breaking up the meat. Take it off the heat, stir in the sumac, and spread the filling on a plate to cool.

Cut the other onion in quarters and put it in a food processor with the drained bulgur, the rest of the lamb, the other 1/2 tsp seven-spice, the other 1/4 tsp pepper, 3/4 tsp of the salt and 1 tbsp of the cornstarch. Blitz in 2 batches for 1 to 2 minutes, until it forms a smooth sticky paste. Add a spoonful of cold water if it's crumbly.
Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment. Pour the vegetable oil into a small bowl.

Dip your fingers in the oil. Roll a golf-ball-size piece of the paste, press your thumb into it, and work it into a thin hollow shell. Spoon in about 1 tbsp of the filling, pinch the opening closed, and shape it into an oval with pointed ends. That should be about 16 kibbeh. Set them on the baking sheet.

Bake for 15 minutes, until set and lightly golden but not browned. Let them cool. Refrigerate them for up to 1 day, or freeze them on the tray for 1 hour, then transfer them to a freezer bag for up to 6 months.
Rinse the rice and put it in a small pot with 1 cup water. Bring to a boil, then cover and cook over low heat for 20 minutes, until soft.
Whisk the yogurt, the remaining 2 tbsp cornstarch and 1 tsp of the salt in a large pot, off the heat. Stir in the rice and any water left in its pot.
Put the pot over medium-high heat and stir constantly in one direction for about 8 minutes, until the sauce comes to a boil. Turn the heat to low.
Add the kibbeh and simmer gently for 10 minutes, stirring now and then. If they're frozen, simmer for 15 minutes. Add a splash of water if the sauce gets too thick.
Melt the butter in a small skillet over medium-low heat. Add the garlic, minced, and the cilantro and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Stir the garlic and cilantro into the pot with the dried mint. Take the pot off the heat.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve in shallow bowls, hot or cold.

To store, refrigerate the finished dish in a covered container for up to 3 days. Warm it in a pot over low heat with a splash of water. Don't freeze the finished dish, since the yogurt sauce separates. Freeze the baked kibbeh on their own, as in step 6.
advance_prep_notes: make, bake and shape the kibbeh up to a day ahead, or freeze them
method_notes: The lead (Zaatar and Zaytoun, 5.0 from 6) fills a lamb and bulgur shell with spiced meat, bakes it to firm it, then simmers it in a rice and cornstarch yogurt sauce finished with garlic, cilantro and mint. The page's 1500 g of yogurt looks like a typo, so the amount follows The Matbakh and Hadia's versions, scaled to 4. Pine nuts are left out to keep it nut-free. Honest total is about 2 hours; the kibbeh can be made ahead and frozen.
